Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company v. Dalian Jinshiji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract

Ruling Summary

Creditor's rights are relative rights, and relativity is the foundation of creditor's rights. Therefore, creditor's rights are, in legal nature, rights against persons. A debt is a legal relationship between specific parties, and both the creditor and the debtor are specific. The creditor may only seek performance from the specific debtor, and the debtor is only obligated to perform to the specific creditor. Even if the creditor's right cannot be realized due to the act of a third party who is not a party to the contract, the creditor cannot, by virtue of the effect of the creditor's right, request the third party to remove the obstruction, nor can it, without legal basis, break through the principle of relativity of contract to require the third party to assume joint and several liability for the debt.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 39

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company, domiciled at No. 90 Changxing Street, Shahekou District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Wanyou, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Changsheng, lawyer of Liaoning Yuande Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Shicai, male, Han nationality, born in August 1955, teacher at Dalian Naval Academy.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Dalian Jinshiji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 52 Yingbin Road, Shahekou District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Zhen, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Meng Bing, lawyer of Beijing Jingdu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Bo, lawyer of Beijing Jingdu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 6-2, No. 142 Qinguan Street, Xigang District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Teng Baoyu, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lu Haiyun, lawyer of Liaoning Yatai Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 139 Shenyang Road, Xigang District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Pan Guoyan, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Song Zisheng, Legal Counsel of the Company.

In the case concerning a dispute over a construction project contract between the appellant Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company (hereinafter referred to as Bohai Company) and the appellant Dalian Jinshiji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinshiji Company), and the respondents Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baoyu Group) and Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baoyu Company), Bohai Company and Jinshiji Company appealed against the civil judgment (2006) Liao Min Yi Chu Zi No. 3 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court. After acceptance, the Supreme People's Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on May 17, 2007. The agents ad litem of Bohai Company, Xu Changsheng and Lu Shicai, the agents ad litem of Jinshiji Company, Meng Bing and Liu Bo, the agent ad litem of Baoyu Company, Lu Haiyun, and the agent ad litem of Baoyu Group, Song Zisheng, attended the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance:

On March 5, 2001, Bohai Company and Baoyu Group entered into a Construction Project Contract, agreeing that Bohai Company would construct Building Nos. 2 and 4 of the high-rise residential buildings of the Dalian New Century Residential Community (later renamed New Century Homeland, hereinafter referred to as New Century Homeland). The contract price was RMB 44.4 million (settled based on actual quantities). The quality grade of the project was to be provincial excellent project. The economic expenditure required for the quality grade: implement the relevant government document Da Jian Zi [1989] No. 32. Payment method for the project price: bank transfer check according to the construction progress image, the progress payment to be paid within one week, and 98% of the total construction cost to be paid within 30 days after completion of the project. If Baoyu Group failed to settle within 30 days after receiving the completion report from Bohai Company, interest on the overdue project payment would be paid from the 31st day at the planned loan interest rate of the construction enterprise, and liability for breach of contract would be assumed.

On March 18, 2001, Bohai Company and Baoyu Group signed a Supplemental Agreement, stipulating that: the contract price for the construction and installation works (including basement works) of Building Nos. 2 and 4 of the New Century Homeland to be undertaken by Bohai Company was tentatively set at RMB 44.4 million. Bohai Company agreed to advance funds for construction up to the sixth floor above ground. At that time, Baoyu Group would pay Bohai Company 10% of the contract price as project payment. When Bohai Company reached the 15th floor of the main structure, Baoyu Group would pay another 10% of the contract price. Upon topping out of the main structure, Baoyu Group would pay another 10% of the contract price. Upon completion of external wall plastering, tile laying, painting, etc., another 10% of the contract price would be paid. Upon full completion of the project, after Bohai Company had organized and submitted all completion archive materials, and the project had been accepted by the relevant departments according to the quality grade agreed in the contract, Bohai Company would have to remove all personnel, materials, and equipment from the site. Baoyu Group would then pay another 8% of the contract price to Bohai Company, with the remaining 2% retained as a quality warranty deposit, to be returned after the statutory warranty period expired. The remaining 50% of the project payment would be paid by Baoyu Group to Bohai Company in the form of commercial housing units in the project at RMB 7,800 per square meter. The commercial housing units used to offset the project payment were designated as Type B units (202.20 square meters) and Type C units (151.57 square meters) on the 6th to 14th floors of Building No. 2. The project quality must reach provincial excellence. No water leakage or seepage was permitted on the roof, walls, kitchen, bathroom, or flower terrace. If any seepage occurred, Bohai Company would compensate Baoyu Group RMB 30,000 per location, to be deducted from the project final account and warranty deposit. The commencement date of Bohai Company's construction was March 1, 2001.

On July 14, 2001, Bohai Company and Baoyu Group signed a Work Stoppage Report, which stated: 1. Because the construction unit failed to pay the progress payment in a timely manner as stipulated in the contract, Bohai Company owed huge sums of material costs to the mixing station and steel bar suppliers, and the mixing station and steel bar suppliers had stopped supplying concrete and steel bars to Bohai Company. 2. Because the garage plan and masonry plan had not been finalized, the steel bar squad (36 persons) that entered the site on June 28, 2001, and the masonry brick-laying squad (38 persons) that entered the site on July 2, 2001, had been in a standby state and all left before July 14, 2001. 3. All site construction personnel had not received wages since the start of this project, and the steel bar and steel formwork sections went on strike for three days. In view of the above, the project could not proceed normally, and Bohai Company was forced to completely stop construction and give leave to workers starting from July 15, 2001.

On September 6, 2002, to ensure that the loan for the New Century Homeland project was used exclusively for the project, Baoyu Company entered into a Fund Supervision Agreement with the Shahekou Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Dalian (hereinafter referred to as Shahekou Sub-branch).

On November 26, 2002, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into an Agreement, stipulating: 1. The Construction Project Contract signed between Baoyu Company and Bohai Company in March 2001 provided that Bohai Company would construct Building Nos. 2 and 4 of the New Century Homeland. The originally agreed construction period was from March 18, 2001, to December 31, 2001. However, due to insufficient funds from Baoyu Company, the project was suspended midway, causing certain economic losses to Bohai Company. 2. Given that Baoyu Company's funds had now been secured, through negotiation, Baoyu Company agreed to compensate Bohai Company for its losses by providing a consumption card worth RMB 800,000 for the Dalian Baoyuyuan Hotel and one commercial housing unit, Room 1 on the 10th floor of Unit 1, Building No. 4 of the New Century Homeland. ... 5. Upon signing this Agreement, Bohai Company shall immediately re-enter the New Century Homeland construction site to resume work, and guarantee completion by September 30, 2003, for delivery to Baoyu Company. Upon signing this Agreement, Bohai Company shall no longer demand any compensation from Baoyu Company and shall waive the right to pursue Baoyu Company's liability for breach of contract arising prior to the signing of this Agreement.

On December 1, 2002, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into an Agreement, stipulating: 1. In the performance of the construction contract signed with Baoyu Company by Bohai Company, due to Baoyu Company's insufficient funds, the project was in a state of prolonged suspension. Bohai Company suffered significant losses due to the suspension. The amount of losses claimed by Bohai Company was: labor costs, material costs, and machinery costs of RMB 7,707,021.14, and management fees of RMB 1,541,404.23. In addition, Bohai Company demanded that Baoyu Company bear liquidated damages of RMB 1.332 million. The total claim amount for the above three items was RMB 10,580,425.37. 2. Although Bohai Company's losses were caused by Baoyu Company's failure to pay project funds on time, Bohai Company was considerate of Baoyu Company's difficulties and agreed to reduce the claim amount to RMB 5.5 million, and guaranteed not to make any other compensation or claim demands. 3. The said RMB 5.5 million in compensation shall be paid in a lump sum to Bohai Company within one week after the signing of this Agreement. If Baoyu Company fails to pay the full compensation on time, Bohai Company reserves the right to suspend work again. Any losses caused by resuspension due to Baoyu Company's failure to pay compensation on time shall be fully borne by Baoyu Company.

On December 5, 2002, Bohai Company, Baoyu Company, and the project's supervision company, Dalian Hongda Construction Supervision Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongda Company), signed a Work Resumption Report, which stated that the project funds were now fully in place and winter construction would commence immediately.

On June 27, 2003, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into a Supplemental Agreement, stipulating: Baoyu Company contracted to Bohai Company the construction of all underfloor heating systems for Buildings 1 to 4 of the New Century Homeland and the basement level garage building. The underfloor heating project included all related underfloor heating systems and cement surface layer works from after the main pipe branch, covering an area of approximately 40,000 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 78 per square meter (including cement mortar leveling layer). The total project cost was tentatively set at RMB 3.12 million, to be settled based on actual quantities after project completion. Baoyu Company would first pay RMB 700,000 in project funds, and the remaining project funds would be offset by one commercial housing unit on the east side of the 6th floor of Building 2 of the New Century Homeland (area 245.94 square meters), at a unit price of RMB 8,500 per square meter. The underground garage on the first basement level had a construction area of approximately 4,200 square meters, at a tentative unit price of RMB 1,500 per square meter, to be settled based on actual quantities after project completion. For the construction of the underground garage for Buildings 2 and 4 (approximately 2,100 square meters), Baoyu Company would pay 50% of the project funds, and the remaining 50% would be offset by Baoyu Company with housing units: housing units located on the 6th to 14th floors of the middle unit of Building 2, with an area of 178.32 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 7,800 per square meter. For the construction of the underground garage between Buildings 1 and 3 (approximately 2,100 square meters), Party A (Baoyu Company) would pay 55% of the project funds, and the remaining 45% would be offset by Baoyu Company with the second commercial housing unit on the east side of Type C unit on the 6th floor of Building 2, with an area of 178.32 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 7,800 per square meter.

On August 29, 2003, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into an Agreement regarding the underfloor heating project for Building 1 and the finishing works for Buildings 2 and 4, stipulating: 1. Both parties shall verify the remaining quantities of work. 2. Baoyu Company shall disburse to Bohai Company the last progress payment before completion, totaling RMB 1 million, within three days after signing the agreement. 3. Bohai Company undertakes to complete the finishing works as required by Baoyu Company with quality and quantity guaranteed, promising that, except for the public construction and basement parts, Building 2 will be handed over on September 20, 2003, and Building 4 will be handed over on September 5, 2003. Baoyu Company shall confirm and return all work quantity visa sheets to Bohai Company before handover. 4. During the performance of this agreement, if Bohai Company's construction is affected by force majeure, Baoyu Company's reasons, or reasons of Baoyu Company's subcontractors, causing delays, Baoyu Company shall pay Bohai Company compensation of RMB 20,000 per day of delay, reflected in work quantity visa forms. If Bohai Company delays handover, a penalty of RMB 20,000 per day of delay shall be imposed. ... 7. As agreed in the contract between the parties, within 30 days after completion, Bohai Company shall submit completion materials and acceptance reports to Baoyu Company, and the project quality shall reach provincial excellence.

On April 9, 2004, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into an Agreement, stipulating: 1. From the date of signing this agreement to April 9, 2004, Baoyu Company guarantees to pay Bohai Company RMB 250,000 in project funds, and a further RMB 250,000 by April 16, 2004. For each day of delay in the above two payments, Baoyu Company shall pay Bohai Company a penalty of RMB 20,000. 2. After this payment, Bohai Company guarantees to complete all works by May 6, 2004, to meet the original contract quality standards and pass acceptance by Baoyu Company and the supervisor, and to remove all personnel, machinery, and equipment from the New Century Homeland construction site. For each day of delay in the above, Bohai Company shall pay Baoyu Company a penalty of RMB 15,000. If the delay is caused by Baoyu Company or its entrusted construction team, the construction period shall be extended for each day of delay.

On May 1, 2004, Hongda Company issued a Project Quality Assessment Report for Buildings 2 and 4 of the New Century Homeland, the "Conclusion on the Unit Project" column of which stated: "The work content specified in the design documents and the contract has been completed. Mandatory standards were strictly implemented throughout the construction process. The foundation and the main structure are safe and reliable, with no quality hazards, meeting functional use requirements. The appearance quality meets the inspection and evaluation standards. The scoring rates are: building (indoor/outdoor) 90.42%, plumbing and heating 99.13%, electrical 96%, ventilation and air conditioning 90%, elevator 100%, with a weighted total scoring rate of 106.73%. The unit project is comprehensively assessed as excellent."

On May 8, 2004, the construction of Buildings 2 and 4 by Bohai Company was completed.

On May 18, 2004, Baoyu Company issued the Completion Acceptance Report for Buildings 2 and 4 of the New Century Homeland. The "Completion Acceptance Opinion" column of the report stated: "The acceptance group unanimously discussed and considered that the project has completed the content specified in the design drawings and the contract. The project quality complies with mandatory standards. The foundation and main structure have no safety hazards. The functional use meets technical requirements. The technical engineering archives and supervision archives are complete, the guarantee materials are complete, and the quality inspection standards are accurate. The acceptance of the New Century Homeland project is approved." On May 30, 2004, Bohai Company, Baoyu Company, and Hongda Company signed the Unit Project Completion and Handover Certificate for Buildings 2 and 4 of the New Century Homeland. The "Acceptance Opinion" part of the certificate stated: "After inspection and acceptance of the on-site physical objects and technical data, it is determined that the project meets the design and construction code requirements, meets mandatory standards and regulatory requirements, meets functional use requirements, and the comprehensive project quality is assessed as excellent. Acceptance is approved."

On November 15, 2004, Baoyu Company issued a Statement on the Settlement of Project Funds, stating: "The New Century Homeland Building 2 and 4 residential project contracted by Baoyu Company was undertaken by Bohai Company. The project has been completed by Bohai Company in accordance with Baoyu Company's scope of works, quality requirements, and schedule requirements. Both parties are currently conducting a final settlement for the specific quantities of work. The quantity calculation is complex. It is expected that the settlement will be completed before the end of the year."

On November 17, 2004, Baoyu Company issued a receipt, which stated: "Today received from Bohai Company the settlement documents for the heating works of New Century Buildings 1 to 4, including 4 copies of the settlement document for the underfloor heating project from the main pipe branch (vertical pipe to water separator part), the total price in the settlement documents being RMB 798,664.00, and the settlement documents for the main vertical heating pipes of Buildings 2 and 4, the total price in the settlement documents being RMB 180,759.00. Our company still needs to review and confirm the settlement. This amount, after review and confirmation, will be paid to your company together with the outstanding project payments for Buildings 2 and 4, the claim amount (RMB 5.5 million as per agreement), and the compensation housing unit (one unit)."

In December 2004, the New Century Homeland Building 2 and 4 project constructed by Bohai Company was awarded the title of 2004 Liaoning Province Excellent Main Structure Project.

On January 17, 2005, the Dalian Municipal Construction Project Quality Supervision Station issued a Rectification Notice, which stated: Project name: New Century Homeland Buildings 1 to 4 and underground garage. Issues: (1) Fire protection procedures and wall reform special fund procedures are incomplete; (2) The municipal engineering of the residential complex is not completed; (3) The public construction project (indoor/outdoor) is not completed; (4) Some water grates in the basement are not installed, partial decorative surface layer is moldy; (5) indoor and outdoor wall cracks; (6) The window sill height of some north-side windows is less than 0.9 meters, lacking protective measures; (7) Some door openings are not sealed properly; (8) Cold penetration phenomena exist in individual rooms; (9) Roof waterproof detailing is not properly handled, with warping phenomena; (10) Barrier-free facilities are incomplete; (11) Column reinforcement of the top floor of the underground garage is exposed, not treated; (12) Technical engineering archive materials are not complete.

On May 18, 2005, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company signed the Bohai Construction New Century Homeland Project Audit Table, which stated: The total project cost after audit is RMB 48,321,289.00, of which the undisputed part for Building 2 is RMB 29,191,563.00 (main structure part RMB 27,691,044.00), for Building 4 is RMB 13,399,132.00 (main structure part RMB 12,278,635.00), garage pile works RMB 493,188.00, underfloor heating RMB 3,018,256.00, material storage fee for Party A-supplied materials RMB 12,330.00, and the disputed part is RMB 2,206,890.00.

On May 20, 2005, Baoyu Company issued a Letter of Commitment, which stated: "Because the Supplemental Agreement signed between Baoyu Company and Bohai Company provided for offsetting part of the project payment with housing units, but the property titles for the houses in this development project cannot currently be obtained, Baoyu Company commits to complete within six months the relevant procedures required for obtaining property titles for the project houses, such as land certificate, sales permit, and project completion record certificate, so as to facilitate the acquisition of property titles for the housing units offsetting Bohai Company's project payment. Otherwise, Baoyu Company agrees to pay Bohai Company the project payment in cash. Regarding the project payment matters, Baoyu Company agrees to treat the remaining RMB 8 million of the RMB 25 million transferred from Baoyu Company to Bohai Company's account on November 28, 2002, as project payment to Bohai Company. The RMB 17 million is otherwise used by Baoyu Company and cannot be considered as project payment to Bohai Company. The project payment owed by Baoyu Company to Bohai Company will be arranged for payment separately."

Shahekou Sub-branch made the following fund transfers to Bohai Company: as recorded on the transfer checks, the payee was Bohai Company for the following amounts: RMB 25 million on November 28, 2002; RMB 1 million on April 3, 2003; RMB 2 million on April 11, 2003; RMB 1 million on May 13, 2003; RMB 3.5 million on July 14, 2003; and RMB 1 million on September 2, 2003, totaling RMB 33.5 million. In addition, on March 18, 2003, Shahekou Sub-branch transferred RMB 5.5 million, with the transfer check indicating the payee as You Jun; on April 7, 2003, it transferred RMB 2 million, with the transfer check indicating the payee as Baoyu Company. These two payments were recorded in Shahekou Sub-branch's fund supervision ledger as being used by Bohai Company. On April 10, 2003, a transfer of RMB 300,000 was made, with the transfer check indicating the payee as Dalian Electric Power Bureau Inner-City Power Supply Bureau, and in Shahekou Sub-branch's fund supervision ledger, the user was recorded as Bohai Company and another construction unit, Yongjia Company. On February 28, 2003, Bohai Company issued a confirmation letter to Shahekou Sub-branch, confirming that it had received project funds of RMB 25 million from Baoyu Company on November 29, 2002. During the trial of the first instance, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company confirmed that after Bohai Company received the RMB 25 million, it returned RMB 17 million to Baoyu Company.

During the trial of the first instance, it was jointly confirmed by Bohai Company and Baoyu Company that the total amount of project funds paid by Baoyu Company during the construction process was RMB 19,986,030.00, of which RMB 16.95 million was transferred through Shahekou Sub-branch, and the value of materials provided amounted to RMB 3,036,030.00. Bohai Company also received consumption cards valued at RMB 1.042 million from Baoyu Company.

It was further found that the business license copy of Bohai Company indicated: its principal business included first-class civil engineering construction, maintenance, interior and exterior decoration, etc. Its registered capital was RMB 19.01 million. Baoyu Company obtained the "Construction Engineering Construction Permit" on September 27, 2001. On April 23, 2004, Baoyu Company issued a "Statement Regarding the Application for the Construction Engineering Construction Permit," which stated: "In April 2001, our company independently went to the Dalian Municipal Construction Committee to apply for the Construction Engineering Construction Permit and ultimately obtained the permit in our company's name. Now that the construction project is eligible for applying for a sales permit, because our company obtained the Construction Engineering Construction Permit in our name, Golden Century Company lacks this permit and cannot apply for a sales permit. To expedite the sales permit application, our company will actively cooperate with Golden Century Company to change the Construction Engineering Construction Permit to Golden Century Company's name." Thereafter, Golden Century Company obtained the "Construction Engineering Construction Permit." Article 3 of Document No. Da Jian Zi [1989] 32, issued by the Dalian Urban and Rural Construction Committee on November 15, 1989, regarding strengthening the quality veto power and implementing pricing based on quality with rewards for good and penalties for poor quality, stipulated: "For projects rated as provincial-level or above excellent projects, the construction unit shall pay 2% of the total project cost to the construction company as a reward." The three parties had no objection to the authenticity of the document, but Baoyu Company argued that it could not serve as the basis for rewarding Bohai Company.

It was further found that on October 8, 2000, Baoyu Group and Golden Century Company entered into the "Joint Development Agreement," stipulating: Golden Century Company and Baoyu Group would jointly develop and construct New Century Homes within the premises of Unit 39023 of the Second Star Sea Station, Shahekou District, Dalian. Golden Century Company would handle the relevant procedures for the project land and bear all costs. Baoyu Group and Golden Century Company would jointly apply for the "Construction Permit" and related procedures, with Baoyu Group bearing all costs from project commencement to completion. Baoyu Group would pay RMB 30 million to Golden Century Company to settle the debts incurred by Golden Century Company in handling the preliminary procedures for the project. Golden Century Company would repay the principal and interest of the RMB 30 million paid by Baoyu Group in the form of real estate within the profit-sharing ratio of the joint development project, increasing Baoyu Group's profit-sharing ratio accordingly. Golden Century Company would receive 35% of the project's saleable area, and Baoyu Group would receive 65%. Golden Century Company would be responsible for geological survey, engineering design, and engineering supervision. Baoyu Group and Golden Century Company would jointly be responsible for project command, leadership, and property sales, with costs borne by both parties in proportion to their shares. Both parties would jointly select construction teams, and the project budget would be jointly approved by both parties. During the joint development, Baoyu Group could use the project's land certificate or semi-finished houses as collateral for loans, and the loaned amount should be placed in an account recognized by both parties, managed jointly, ensuring all funds were used for the joint development project, with Baoyu Group responsible for repayment. If work stoppage occurred after project commencement due to reasons attributable to Golden Century Company, Golden Century Company would pay the construction unit compensation for idle labor losses; if due to reasons attributable to Baoyu Group, Baoyu Group would pay such compensation.

On October 15, 2002, Baoyu Group and Golden Century Company entered into the "Supplemental Agreement to the Joint Development Agreement," stipulating: The profit-sharing ratio for the joint development project was adjusted to Golden Century Company receiving 33.5% of the total project area, and Baoyu Group receiving 66.5%. The project would be jointly managed by both parties with joint offices. Baoyu Group would bear all supervision costs. Both parties would jointly select project contractors, subcontractors, material suppliers, etc., through bidding (except for six contracts already signed by Baoyu Group before this supplemental agreement took effect, including earthwork contracts, construction contracts, weak current contracts, fire protection contracts, and supervision contracts). All contracts, agreements, and budgets related to the joint development project must be reviewed by both parties and must have a written confirmation letter signed by authorized personnel of both parties; otherwise, no external contracts could be signed or payments made. Both parties established a joint loan account at Shahekou Sub-branch, account number 202001040002036. On November 1 of the same year, Baoyu Group and Golden Century Company entered into the "Supplemental Agreement on Joint Account Management," stipulating: To better manage the use of loans and ensure dedicated funds for specific purposes, both parties established a dedicated loan account at Shahekou Sub-branch, account number 303901040014155. The "Commercial Housing Sales Permit" for this project was issued in the name of Golden Century Company.

Golden Century Company obtained the "Construction Land Planning Permit" for New Century Homes on June 26, 2000, the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" on December 12, 2000, the "Construction Project Planning Permit" on August 16, 2001, and the "Commercial Housing Pre-Sale Permit" on May 13, 2004. All sales of New Century Homes were conducted under Golden Century Company's name in the form of sales contracts.

Golden Century Company published a solemn statement in the Dalian Daily, stating: The development rights and ownership of New Century Homes belong to Golden Century Company, and any transactions involving the project (including using project homes to offset project payments or debts) are illegal.

It was also found that when Baoyu Group signed the agreement with Golden Century Company on October 8, 2000, its name was Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. It changed its name to Baoyu Group on February 5, 2002, with its legal representative being Teng Baoyu, later replaced by the current legal representative Pan Guoyan. On July 8, 2002, Baoyu Group applied to the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce to re-establish Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. using Baoyu Company's original qualification certificate. In its application report, Baoyu Group stated: "If any issues regarding creditor's rights and debts arise, because the original real estate development company had increased its registered capital to RMB 120 million before changing to Baoyu Group, any creditor's rights or debts at this stage can be assumed by Baoyu Group. Creditor's rights and debts at other stages will be assumed by Baoyu Real Estate. The re-registered Baoyu Real Estate has a registered capital of RMB 15 million, and we guarantee that it will not harm the interests of others regarding creditor's rights and debts." On August 8 of the same year, Baoyu Group and its subsidiary, Dalian Baoyu Construction Co., Ltd., jointly invested to re-register Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., which had exactly the same name as the pre-name-change Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

Bohai Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that on March 5, 2001, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into a "Construction Project Construction Contract," under which Bohai Company undertook the construction of Buildings 2# and 4# of the New Century Homes residential community. Bohai Company performed its construction obligations, and both parties conducted the project completion settlement, but Baoyu Company failed to pay the project funds as stipulated in the contract. It requested: 1. An order that Baoyu Company pay the outstanding project funds of RMB 34,633,923.88 plus interest from May 18, 2005, until the date of full payment; 2. An order that Baoyu Company pay an excellent project reward of RMB 966,425.00 plus interest from May 18, 2005, until the date of payment; 3. An order that Baoyu Company deliver to Bohai Company one unit of commercial housing at New Century Homes, Building 4#, Unit 1, Floor 10, Room 1 (estimated value of RMB 800,000); 4. An order that Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company jointly assume responsibility for paying the project funds; 5. An order that the joint development unit, Golden Century Company, assume joint and several liability.

Baoyu Company responded: 1. The total cost of this project was RMB 48,321,289.00. Baoyu Company had paid Bohai Company cash project funds of RMB 16.95 million, material payments of RMB 3,036,030.00, consumption cards used to offset project funds of RMB 1.4 million (totaling RMB 21,386,030.00), and housing offsets totaling RMB 22,736,666.00. Without deducting 2% of the total project cost as a project quality warranty deposit, Baoyu Company still owed project funds of only RMB 4,198,593.00. Bohai Company must submit all completion data and acceptance reports to Baoyu Company in accordance with the agreement, after which Baoyu Company could pay the outstanding project funds of RMB 3,232,167.22 (after deducting the 2% project quality warranty deposit of RMB 966,425.78). 2. According to the agreement, Baoyu Company could only deliver housing valued at RMB 1,923,978.50 to Bohai Company to offset the outstanding project funds, and could not pay in cash. 3. Since Bohai Company had not yet submitted completion data and acceptance reports to Baoyu Company, Baoyu Company should not pay interest on the outstanding project funds. 4. Golden Century Company should be jointly liable with Baoyu Company for paying the aforesaid project funds (including housing offsets) to Bohai Company. 5. Bohai Company's claim for project funds of RMB 798,664.00 for the geothermal work was without basis. 6. Bohai Company's claim for liquidated damages for delay was inconsistent with the facts, and this claim had exceeded the statutory two-year statute of limitations period. 7. Regarding Bohai Company's claim for RMB 966,425.00 in reward funds: Although the Dalian municipal document stipulated: "For projects rated as provincial-level or above excellent projects, the construction unit shall pay 2% of the total project cost to the construction company as a reward," the certificate provided by Bohai Company only proved that the main structure it constructed was rated as a provincial-level excellent project, not that the entire project was so rated, and thus did not meet the document's requirements. The claim for RMB 966,425.00 in reward funds was not sustainable. 8. Bohai Company had previously promised to waive its claim for one unit of commercial housing at New Century Homes, Building 4#, Unit 1, Floor 10, Room 1. After both parties signed an agreement to this effect, Baoyu Company affixed its seal, but Bohai Company took the agreement for its own sealing and did not return it to Baoyu Company. Therefore, Bohai Company should abide by its commitment to waive the claim for this house. 9. Bohai Company breached the contract and should pay liquidated damages of RMB 8.34 million, including RMB 2.04 million for quality issues, RMB 4.86 million for delay, and RMB 1.44 million for failing to deliver completion data. In summary, Baoyu Company owed Bohai Company RMB 3,232,167.22 in project funds, and Bohai Company should pay Baoyu Company liquidated damages totaling RMB 8.34 million. It requested the court to dismiss Bohai Company's claims and order Bohai Company to immediately deliver completion data and acceptance reports to Baoyu Company, and pay the remaining liquidated damages of RMB 4.15 million. 10. The project in question was a joint development between Baoyu Company and Golden Century Company, and the project was co-owned by both parties, with no distribution of project interests. Therefore, Baoyu Company requested the court to order that Baoyu Company and Golden Century Company jointly pay the above project funds to Bohai Company, and that Golden Century Company should register the houses obtained by Bohai Company as offsets for project funds under Bohai Company's name as soon as possible.

Golden Century Company responded: 1. Bohai Company's request for Golden Century Company to assume joint and several liability for paying project funds was based on neither factual nor legal grounds, constituting an abuse of the right to sue. 2. The amount of outstanding project funds claimed by Bohai Company had no factual basis. The actual amount of project funds paid by Baoyu Company was RMB 39 million. The amount recognized by both Bohai Company and Baoyu Company was not the actual amount of project funds paid, but rather the amount after deducting voluntary loans and other transactions between Bohai Company and Baoyu Company. After receiving the project funds, Bohai Company lent funds back to Baoyu Company. Bohai Company's claim for repayment of those loans should be handled in a separate case and was not within the scope of this trial. It was not suitable to consolidate the cases, and Bohai Company should file a separate lawsuit. 3. The "Supplemental Agreement" dated March 18, 2001, between Bohai Company and Baoyu Company, which used houses to offset project funds, violated relevant laws and regulations, harmed the interests of Golden Century Company and the lending bank, and should be declared invalid. 4. On one hand, Baoyu Company argued that it should not pay Bohai Company any more project funds and filed a counterclaim for over RMB 8.34 million in liquidated damages; on the other hand, it requested that Golden Century Company assume joint liability for paying project funds. This was contradictory and aimed at shifting liability to Golden Century Company. It requested the court to dismiss Bohai Company's claims and protect the legitimate rights and interests of Golden Century Company. At the same time, Golden Century Company reserved the right to claim damages from Bohai Company for losses caused by the abuse of the right to sue.

Baoyu Group did not provide a written defense but stated in court that it agreed to be added as a co-defendant and agreed with Baoyu Company's defense. Baoyu Group acknowledged that the project constructed by Bohai Company had been completed and delivered, and agreed to jointly assume responsibility with Golden Century Company for paying the project funds.

The court of first instance held that the "Joint Development Agreement" and "Supplemental Agreement to Joint Development" entered into between Baoyu Company and Golden Century Company, and the "Construction Project Construction Contract" entered into between Bohai Company and Baoyu Company, reflected the true intentions of the parties, contained no illegal acts, and were legally valid. Bohai Company had performed its construction obligations under the contract, and both parties had conducted a settlement. Baoyu Company should also perform its contractual obligations and pay the outstanding project funds and interest to Bohai Company.

The court of first instance identified the following key issues in dispute:

(1) The issue of the project cost for the disputed portion (branch pipes) of the geothermal work.

The court of first instance held: On June 27, 2003, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company entered into a "Supplemental Agreement," stipulating that the entire geothermal work for Buildings 1# to 4# of New Century Homes would be constructed by Bohai Company, with the agreed geothermal price being RMB 3.12 million. In the New Century Homes Engineering Review Form dated May 18, 2005, both parties jointly confirmed the geothermal project cost to be RMB 3,018,256.00. The review form included both the undisputed portion and the disputed portion of the project cost, and should be regarded as the final settlement of the entire project cost by both parties.

Bohai Company claimed that Baoyu Company received the geothermal project completion report in November 2004 and did not respond or raise objections for over a year. However, Bohai Company submitted the completion report to Baoyu Company earlier, and the parties conducted the settlement later. During the settlement, no issue was raised regarding this portion of the project cost. Bohai Company's current claim that the project cost should be increased by RMB 798,664.00 for geothermal work lacked sufficient basis and was not supported.

(2) The issue of the validity of the "Agreement" dated December 1, 2002, between Bohai Company and Baoyu Company.

The court of first instance held: Although the "Agreement" entered into between Baoyu Company and Bohai Company on November 26, 2002, stipulated: "After this agreement is signed, Bohai Company shall no longer demand any compensation from Baoyu Company, and shall waive its right to pursue Baoyu Company's liability for breach of contract arising before this agreement," the agreement in which Bohai Company claimed compensation of RMB 5.5 million was signed later, on December 1, 2002. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company argued that this agreement was made to facilitate the withdrawal of funds from Shahekou Sub-branch, but they failed to provide evidence to support their claim. In a receipt dated November 17, 2004, Baoyu Company again promised to pay Bohai Company the claim amount of RMB 5.5 million. Although Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company raised objections to the receipt, they abandoned their application to verify the seal on the receipt, which should be deemed as an acknowledgment of the seal's authenticity. Therefore, the validity of the agreement dated December 1, 2002, should be upheld. Bohai Company's request for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to pay RMB 5.5 million in compensation should be supported. As for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's argument that Bohai Company's claim for compensation exceeded the statute of limitations, since Baoyu Company promised to pay the compensation on November 17, 2004, and Bohai Company filed this lawsuit with the court of first instance on January 26, 2006, to assert this right, it had not exceeded the statutory limitation period.

(3) The issue of the RMB 966,425.00 reward funds claimed by Bohai Company.

The court of first instance found that: According to the construction contract signed between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group, the scope of Bohai Company's construction included civil engineering, heating, drainage, roof waterproofing, and outdoor supporting works. The parties also stipulated in the construction contract that the economic expenditure for the quality grade of the project shall be executed in accordance with Document No. 1989-32 of the Dalian Construction Quality Supervision Station. The project constructed by Bohai Company was verified by Baoyu Company and the supervising company, and the comprehensive quality assessment was rated as excellent, and it was awarded the title of Liaoning Provincial Excellent Main Structure Project. The project has been delivered for use, and some occupants have already moved in. Although the main project does not include all the works constructed by Bohai Company, such as heating, drainage, roof waterproofing, and outdoor supporting works, after the project was completed and actually put into use, Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company, as the construction units, failed to organize the application for assessment of the quality grade of the entire project. As a result, the responsibility for the inability to determine whether the part of the project constructed by Bohai Company that does not belong to the main structure meets the provincial excellence standard cannot be attributed to Bohai Company. Furthermore, the works other than civil engineering, heating, drainage, roof waterproofing, and outdoor supporting works were not constructed by Bohai Company. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company currently have no evidence to prove that the responsibility for the failure of the entire project to ultimately be confirmed as a provincial excellent project should be borne by Bohai Company. Bohai Company's request for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to pay the quality project award is consistent with the contract between the parties and should be supported. However, because only the main structure part of the project constructed by Bohai Company obtained the provincial excellent project title, Bohai Company's claim that Baoyu Company should pay the award based on the total project cost and also pay interest on such amount is not well-founded and cannot be supported. Based on the detailed breakdown of the total project cost confirmed by both parties, it can be determined that the cost of the main structure works constructed by Bohai Company should be RMB 39,969,679.00 (RMB 27,691,044.00 for Building No. 2 plus RMB 12,278,635.00 for Building No. 4). The provincial excellent project award payable by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company is RMB 7,993,935.80. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company argued that the "Liaoning Provincial Excellent Main Structure Project Certificate" of Bohai Company only evidenced that the main structure of the project was excellent, not that the entire project was excellent, and that they had not promised a reward, so they should not pay the quality project award. This argument is inconsistent with the facts and was not supported by the court of first instance.

(IV) Whether Jinshiji Company should bear the responsibility for paying the project funds to Bohai Company.

The court of first instance found that: First, although the construction contract was signed between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company, Jinshiji Company was a joint developer of the project constructed by Bohai Company. The joint development interests of Jinshiji Company and Baoyu Group had not yet been divided. Moreover, the land use certificate, sales permit, etc. for the New Century Garden project were all processed in the name of Jinshiji Company, and the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" for selling the New Century Garden project real estate was also signed in the name of Jinshiji Company. Although Jinshiji Company did not sign the construction contract with Bohai Company, it enjoyed the rights to the project constructed by Bohai Company and obtained benefits from the contract. Therefore, Jinshiji Company should bear the corresponding obligations under the contract. Jinshiji Company argued that imposing joint and several liability for the payment of project funds on it broke the principle of privity of contract and had no factual or legal basis, and this argument could not be supported. Second, in the "Joint Construction Agreement" and "Supplemental Agreement to the Joint Construction Agreement," Baoyu Group, Baoyu Company, and Jinshiji Company stipulated that they would jointly select the construction team, jointly manage the New Century Garden project, and the loan for the New Century Garden project would be placed in an account jointly recognized by the parties and managed jointly. Although Bohai Company was not the construction team jointly selected by Baoyu Group and Jinshiji Company, in the supplemental agreement between Jinshiji Company and Baoyu Group and during the performance of the construction contract between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company, Jinshiji Company had recognized the construction contract signed between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company. When Bohai Company requested funds from Baoyu Group during construction, Jinshiji Company also signed and sealed the "Payment Request Report," indicating that Jinshiji Company had actually participated in the performance of the construction contract. Jinshiji Company argued that the above could not serve as grounds for assuming joint and several liability, but this argument lacked a sufficient basis and was also not supported. Third, according to the joint construction agreement signed by Baoyu Group and Jinshiji Company, they jointly invested and jointly obtained benefits. Their joint construction behavior should be characterized as a partnership in law, and partners should be liable for partnership debts. Therefore, although Jinshiji Company did not directly sign the construction contract with Bohai Company, it could not be exempted from its obligation to pay project funds to Bohai Company in accordance with the law. Jinshiji Company should bear joint and several liability for the project funds owed by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company. As for Jinshiji Company's argument that imposing joint and several liability on it without the approval of the project completion settlement between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company deprived it of rights corresponding to the liability it bore. Because the construction contract was signed between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group, the project cost settlement between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group was valid. Jinshiji Company did not object to the project cost during the litigation and also did not provide evidence to prove that the settlement harmed the interests of Jinshiji Company. Therefore, Jinshiji Company's non-recognition of the project settlement between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group was without basis. Moreover, the judgment in this case imposed joint and several liability on Jinshiji Company, not direct liability for payment of project funds. During the enforcement of this judgment, if Jinshiji Company assumed joint and several liability for the payment of project funds to Bohai Company by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company under this judgment, Jinshiji Company could either assert its rights against Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company at any time or assert its rights when the joint construction interests were divided between the parties. There was no issue of depriving its rights or harming its interests. Jinshiji Company argued that, as it was not a party to the construction contract, it should not bear the responsibility for paying project funds. This argument was not supported.

Regarding the issues raised by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company that the project constructed by Bohai Company had quality defects, and they requested Bohai Company to pay liquidated damages of RMB 8,349,638.67, deduct the project quality warranty deposit of RMB 966,425.78, and argued that Bohai Company had not submitted completion documents and acceptance reports, so the interest on the outstanding project funds should not be paid. Although the New Century Garden project had not been inspected by the quality inspection department, the project undertaken by Bohai Company had been accepted by Baoyu Company and the supervising unit, the quality was rated as excellent, and it was awarded the Liaoning Provincial Excellent Main Structure Project title. In the "Explanation on the Project Fund Settlement" issued by Baoyu Company on November 15, 2004, it again confirmed that the project quality met the standards agreed in the contract. Now houses have been put up for sale, and some buyers have actually moved in. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company argued that Bohai Company should bear liability for breach of contract on the grounds of quality defects in the project, but this argument lacked a sufficient basis and was not supported. Since Bohai Company and Baoyu Company clarified in the acceptance report that the project file materials were complete, Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's argument that Bohai Company failed to deliver the project on time as agreed in the agreement and did not deliver the completion materials, so the project funds and interest could not be paid, was without factual or legal basis and was not adopted.

Regarding the determination of the amount of project funds paid by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company. From the transfer records of the Shahekou Sub-branch, the project funds paid by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to Bohai Company should be RMB 33.5 million, but Bohai Company actually received RMB 16.95 million in project funds. Neither Bohai Company nor Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company disputed this, so the amount should be determined accordingly. As for Jinshiji Company's argument that the project funds Bohai Company received and then returned to Baoyu Company should be treated as a loan and should not be consolidated with this case for trial, this argument could not be supported. Because after receiving RMB 25 million in project funds from Baoyu Company on November 29, 2002, Bohai Company returned RMB 17 million to Baoyu Company. Jinshiji Company did not bear joint and several liability for this part. As for the issue of whether the hotel consumption cards collected by Bohai Company at Baoyu Company could be recognized as paid project funds. Hotel consumption cards in the amount of RMB 1.042 million that were signed by Bohai Company should be calculated as paid project funds. As for the issue of consumption cards worth RMB 1.2 million paid by Baoyu Company in an agreement with Yida Group. Because Baoyu Company failed to provide evidence to prove that these consumption cards were collected by Bohai Company, Baoyu Company should assert its rights separately. As for the issue of offsetting project funds with real estate. Although there was an agreement between Bohai Company and Baoyu Company to offset project funds with real estate, the real estate in question was jointly constructed by Baoyu Group and Jinshiji Company, and the interests between them had not yet been distributed. Which part of the real estate belonged to Baoyu Group was unclear. Jinshiji Company neither agreed to offset project funds with real estate nor agreed to handle the property ownership procedures for Bohai Company, and the real estate had not actually been delivered to Bohai Company. Therefore, it could not be recognized as paid project funds. In summary, the total project cost of the project constructed by Bohai Company was RMB 48,321,289.00. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company had paid project funds of RMB 21,028,030.00 (RMB 16.95 million transferred from Shahekou Sub-branch, RMB 3,036,030.00 in material discounts, and RMB 1.042 million in hotel consumption cards collected by Bohai Company at Baoyu Company). The outstanding project funds owed by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to Bohai Company were RMB 27,293,259.00.

Regarding Bohai Company's request for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to pay RMB 800,000 in hotel consumption cards and one set of housing units under the agreement dated November 26, 2002. Although Bohai Company and Baoyu Company agreed in the agreement dated November 26, 2002 that Baoyu Company would compensate Bohai Company for its shutdown losses with RMB 800,000 in hotel consumption cards and one set of housing units, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company subsequently signed another shutdown loss compensation agreement on December 1 of the same year. In the December 1 agreement, the parties clearly stipulated that Baoyu Company would pay a lump sum compensation of RMB 5.5 million to Bohai Company. It should be determined that the parties had already modified the shutdown loss compensation provisions of the previous agreement in the later agreement. Bohai Company's claim for this part could not be supported.

Regarding the relationship between Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company. Because when Baoyu Group signed the joint construction agreement and construction contract with Jinshiji Company and Bohai Company, its name was Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., which was completely identical to the name of Baoyu Company that was later registered and established. Moreover, when it changed its name to Baoyu Group and re-registered a new Baoyu Company, it did not notify Jinshiji Company or Bohai Company. Jinshiji Company and Bohai Company believed that the contract was signed and performed by one entity, Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. The court of first instance found that: Bohai Company signed the construction contract and supplemental agreement with Baoyu Group, and Baoyu Group should bear the responsibility for paying the project funds. During the performance of the contract, without notifying the counterparty, Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company allowed Baoyu Company to assume the rights and obligations under the contract. After Bohai Company filed a lawsuit against Baoyu Company as the defendant, Baoyu Company did not object to its status as the defendant. Therefore, in this case, Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company should be jointly regarded as the employer party under the construction contract and should jointly bear the responsibility for paying the project funds.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 52 and 84 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 60 and 114 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and after discussion by the adjudication committee, rendered the following judgment: 1. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, jointly pay to Bohai Company the outstanding project funds of RMB 27,293,259.00, along with interest on such amount calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period from May 18, 2005, until the date this judgment takes effect; 2. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, jointly pay to Bohai Company shutdown losses of RMB 5.5 million; 3. Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, jointly pay to Bohai Company the quality project award of RMB 7,993,935.80; 4. Jinshiji Company shall bear joint and several payment liability for RMB 10,293,259.00 of the RMB 27,293,259.00 in outstanding project funds that Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company are to pay to Bohai Company within 15 days after this judgment takes effect as provided in paragraph 1 of this judgment; 5. Bohai Company's other claims are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 192,333.00 shall be borne jointly by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company.

On December 1, 2006, the court of first instance, by Civil Ruling No. (2006) Liaomin Yichu Zi No. 3, corrected the first-instance judgment regarding "the provincial quality project award payable by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company shall be RMB 7,993,935.80" and "Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company shall jointly pay Bohai Company the quality project award of RMB 7,993,935.80 within 15 days after this judgment takes effect," correcting the quality project award to RMB 799,393.58.

Bohai Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this court, requesting that the second and third items of the judgment be amended to include additional interest; and that the fourth item of the judgment be amended so that Jinshiji Company bears joint and several liability for the full amount of project funds paid by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company to Bohai Company. The facts and reasons are as follows:

(I) Regarding the issue of Jinshiji Company's joint and several liability for the full amount of project funds.

The first-instance judgment found three grounds for Jinshiji Company to bear joint and several liability: First, Jinshiji Company was the true developer, the joint construction interests had not yet been divided, and the joint construction parties should bear joint and several liability to the contractor; Second, Jinshiji Company not only enjoyed the benefits brought by the construction contract but also participated in the performance of the construction contract; Third, the joint construction parties jointly invested, jointly managed, and jointly benefited, which legally constitutes a partnership, i.e., a partnership-type joint operation. In addition, the following reasons should be specifically emphasized:

First, from the nature of the joint construction agreement and supplemental agreement, the contents of the contracts show the true intention of the parties to form a partnership, such as "Party A and Party B shall jointly be responsible for the command and leadership of the project and the sale of the houses," "Party A and Party B shall make entries and settle accounts in a unified account," "Party A and Party B shall jointly select the construction team, and the project budget shall be jointly approved by Party A and Party B," "Party A and Party B shall jointly staff the project construction management, technical management, and project budget personnel," etc. It is apparent that this fully conforms to the legal characteristics of a partnership. Therefore, the relevant legal provisions on partnership should apply to the joint venture parties in this case.

Second, from the perspective of the binding force of the construction contract, Jinshiji Company was not only bound by the joint construction agreement but also by the construction contract, i.e., dual binding, with the two contracts being interdependent and inseparable. Although Jinshiji Company did not sign the construction contract between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group, based on relevant evidence, particularly Jinshiji Company's signing and sealing on the "Payment Request Report," and the fact that the "Construction Permit" and "Commencement Permit" both indicated that Bohai Company was the construction unit, it is sufficiently proven that Bohai Company, as the construction unit involved in the case, was not only fully recognized by Jinshiji Company but Jinshiji Company's specific performance also constituted a practical legal fact. The rights and obligations of the joint venture parties are mutually delegated, and the external division of labor among the partners means that any civil act carried out by one party has the overall external nature of the partners' joint conduct. The effect of an act by one partner should extend to all joint venture partners. It is apparent that Jinshiji Company's arguments such as "two independent contracts" and "privity of contract" cannot stand.

Third, from the perspective of the realization of lawful claims, the law grants construction units the priority right to be compensated for project funds, and this right directly targets the building, which is the result of the contract, i.e., the "Jinyu Xinghai" project in this case. Bohai Company's investment in the project has been fully materialized into the entire project and cannot be separately asserted as a share claim against one joint construction party. The land use certificate, sales permit, sales contracts, etc. involved in the case were all processed in the name of Jinshiji Company, which actually controls the project results. To maximize the realization of the creditor's lawful claims, Jinshiji Company should bear joint and several liability for repaying the outstanding project funds.

Fourth, from the perspective of maintaining the safety and order of the real estate development market, if the principle of privity of contract is solely emphasized, meaning that there is no provision in the construction contract between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company regarding Jinshiji Company's obligation to pay project funds, thereby exempting Jinshiji Company from joint and several liability, this would allow joint construction parties to circumvent the law by maliciously agreeing that the party allocated lower rights or unable to control the project results would independently perform the construction contract, ultimately causing harm to the interests of the contractor. This would inevitably lead to serious consequences of conniving at acts that violate the principles of fairness and justice in civil law and disrupt the real estate development market order.

Fifth, from the perspective of relevant laws and regulations, the General Principles of the Civil Law refers to partnerships between individuals as "individual partnerships," while partnerships between legal persons are regarded as "joint operations." The joint operation involved in this case is clearly a "partnership-type joint operation" among the three types of joint operations, i.e., a partnership between legal persons, where the joint venture parties share common goals and common interests. This characteristic is completely identical to the legal characteristics of an individual partnership. Article 9(2) of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Joint Construction Contracts" stipulates: "Parties to a partnership-type joint operation shall, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations or the contract, bear joint and several liability for the debts of the joint operation." According to this provision, Jinshiji Company should bear joint and several liability for the full amount of outstanding project funds repaid by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company. The first-instance judgment, having determined that Jinshiji Company and Baoyu Group were in a joint and several legal relationship, and without any other contrary reasons, ordered Jinshiji Company to bear "partial" joint and several liability, which is clearly inappropriate.

(II) Regarding the interest on the principal amounts of the shutdown losses and the quality project award.

The nature of both sums is an inseparable part of the entire project funds. If the RMB 5.5 million in shutdown losses had been paid in good faith on December 1, 2002, as agreed in the contract, and the RMB 799,393.58 in quality project award had been paid in good faith in January 2005 when the conditions were met, then both sums, whether used for business or deposited for interest, would naturally generate corresponding profits. Accordingly, Bohai Company's claim that the corresponding interest on the above two sums should be protected is reasonable and lawful, and the reasons are sufficient and should be supported.

Jinshiji Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this court, requesting that the fourth item of the first-instance judgment, i.e., "Dalian Jinshiji Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several payment liability for RMB 10,293,259.00 of the RMB 27,293,259.00 in outstanding project funds that Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. and Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. are to pay to Dalian Bohai Construction General Company within 15 days after this judgment takes effect," be set aside, and that the judgment be amended to find that Jinshiji Company bears no responsibility for the payment of project funds by Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company. The main facts and reasons are as follows:

(I) The first-instance judgment found that the joint construction interests of Jinshiji Company and Baoyu Group had not yet been divided, and that Jinshiji Company obtained benefits from the construction contract and should therefore bear the corresponding obligations under the construction contract. This finding is inconsistent with the facts and has no legal basis.

Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group have already allocated the benefits from the joint construction in the "Joint Construction Agreement" and its supplementary agreements. Jin Century Company was allocated 33.5% of the total floor area of the joint construction project, and Baoyu Group was allocated 66.5%. This is not, as the first-instance judgment determined, a case where the joint construction benefits had not yet been divided. Moreover, the two agreements clearly specify the rights and obligations of Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group, explicitly stating that "Baoyu Group shall bear all expenses required from project commencement to completion (including, of course, construction costs)." The first-instance judgment, however, ordered Jin Century Company to assume joint and several liability for a portion of the project payments. This has neither contractual basis nor legal basis.

The fact that the land use certificate and sales permit for the joint construction project were issued in the name of Jin Century Company, and that the commercial housing sale contracts were signed in the name of Jin Century Company, was an act performed in fulfillment of the obligations under the joint construction agreement between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group. It is unrelated to whether Baoyu Group fulfilled its payment obligations under the construction contract in this case. The cooperative development real estate contract and the construction contract are separate legal relationships. The performance by Jin Century Company under one legal relationship cannot serve as a factual basis for imposing joint and several payment liability on Jin Century Company in another legal relationship in which it is not even a party.

The rights and interests that Jin Century Company enjoys in the development project arise from its cooperative development legal relationship with Baoyu Group. The purpose of its performance was to profit from the joint construction project, not to profit from the construction contract. In fact, Baoyu Group has already obtained all the benefits from the construction contract, and this benefit was obtained as a result of fulfilling its obligations under the joint construction agreement. Therefore, Jin Century Company is not a beneficiary of the construction contract. The fact that Jin Century Company benefited from the joint construction agreement cannot serve as a basis for imposing payment liability under the construction contract. If we follow the logic set forth in the first-instance judgment, the purchasers of units in the joint construction project also accepted the construction results. Could it then be concluded that the purchasers also obtained benefits from the construction contract, thereby imposing joint and several payment liability on them?

A construction contract relationship exists between Bohai Company and Baoyu Group, while a cooperative development real estate contract relationship exists between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group. These are two independent contracts, and there is no joint and several relationship between them. Contracts are relative in nature. As cited by the first-instance judgment, Article 84 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides that debts arising from contracts "create specific rights and obligations only between the parties." Jin Century Company is not a party to the construction contract, has no specific rights and obligations relationship with Bohai Company, and is not obligated to pay project funds to it.

The first-instance judgment, by ordering Jin Century Company to assume payment obligations under the construction contract, violates both the principle of contractual freedom and the principle of fairness under civil law. This is because Jin Century Company has already assumed its corresponding contractual obligations under the cooperative development agreement. Requiring Jin Century Company to also assume obligations that should be borne by the other party to the cooperative development agreement is inequitable.

(2) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that Jin Century Company recognized the construction contract in question and that its seal and signature on the "Payment Request Report" demonstrated its actual participation in the performance of the construction contract. This finding of fact is incorrect.

Although the "Joint Construction Agreement" contains a provision that the parties shall jointly select the construction team, this does not mean that such provision was actually performed. The first-instance judgment also recognized that "Bohai Company was not a construction team jointly selected by Baoyu Group and Jin Century Company." The supplementary agreement does not address the content of the construction contract. There is no written expression of intent in the supplementary agreement that Jin Century Company recognized the six construction contracts. The mention of "except for the earthwork contract, building construction contract, low-voltage electrical contract, fire protection contract, and supervision contract" in the supplementary agreement was intended to mean that, for contracts other than these six, the parties must jointly select through bidding. This was meant to emphasize contracts outside the six, but it does not mean that Jin Century Company recognized these six construction contracts. This is because Baoyu Group signed more than one construction contract for the project in question, and more than one company (including Bohai) signed construction contracts with Baoyu Group. For Jin Century Company to recognize a particular construction contract, a clear written acknowledgment would be required. To interpret the true intent behind the phrase "except for the earthwork contract, building construction contract, low-voltage electrical contract, fire protection contract, and supervision contract," we must look to the true intent of Jin Century Company, as a party to the agreement, at the time of signing. Given the objective fact that there were multiple construction contracts and multiple construction units at that time, Jin Century Company could not and did not express any intent to recognize the construction contract between Baoyu Group and Bohai Company.

Jin Century Company's signature and seal on the "Payment Request Report" were based on its joint construction relationship with Baoyu Group and were acts performed in exercise of its right to supervise funds under the joint construction agreement. The purpose was to ensure that the loan obtained from Shahekou Sub-branch, with Baoyu Group as the borrower, Jin Century Company as the guarantor, and the project as collateral, was used exclusively for the project. Jin Century Company's act of signing and sealing the "Payment Request Report" was an act of exercising its rights in accordance with the agreement and is fundamentally different from performing the construction contract. If we were to follow the logic of the first-instance judgment, the Shahekou Sub-branch, which made the project payment, also reviewed the payment. Could it then be concluded that the bank also participated in the performance of the construction contract, thereby imposing joint and several payment liability on the bank?

(3) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the cooperative development between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group constituted a partnership, thus requiring them to bear joint and several liability externally. This is a finding of fact that is incorrect and an application of law that is improper.

There is certainly no individual partnership between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group, so the provisions of Section 5 "Individual Partnership" under Chapter 2 "Citizens (Natural Persons)" of the General Principles of the Civil Law, which state that "partners shall bear joint and several liability for partnership debts," do not apply. Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group have never expressed any intention to form a partnership, nor have they signed a partnership agreement. Their relationship does not constitute a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons. Even if it were determined that the relationship between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group is a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons, Jin Century Company should still not bear joint and several liability. The prevailing view is that Article 52 of the General Principles of the Civil Law governs partnership-type joint operations between legal persons. The first-instance judgment also relied on this provision as the legal basis for imposing joint and several liability on Jin Century Company. However, it must be pointed out that this article does not provide that partners in a partnership-type joint operation must bear joint and several liability. Rather, it explicitly states that "if joint and several liability is to be borne, it shall be borne in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement of the parties." In other words, joint and several liability for partners arises only when there is a legal provision or an explicit agreement between the parties. This is precisely the difference between a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons and an individual partnership. In an individual partnership, partners inherently bear joint and several liability for partnership debts, whereas in a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons, there are preconditions. In this case, even if it were determined that Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group are in a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons, there is no precondition for Jin Century Company to bear joint and several liability. First, there is no agreement between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group to bear joint and several liability. Second, neither the Construction Law nor the Urban Real Estate Administration Law nor relevant judicial interpretations contain any legal provision that a joint builder should bear joint and several liability for the debts of the other party. The first-instance judgment did not cite any relevant legal basis. It merely stated in a general manner in the "Opinion of the Court of First Instance" section that "partners shall be liable for partnership debts." This argument is untenable. First, this is not a legal provision, and there is no such legal provision. Second, it does not specify what kind of liability is to be borne. If it refers to joint and several liability, then that is precisely a provision under the section on individual partnership in the General Principles of the Civil Law and is not applicable to this case. Therefore, the first-instance judgment confused the distinction between an individual partnership and a partnership-type joint operation between legal persons, constituting an improper application of law.

It should be noted that joint and several liability is a very significant form of civil liability. Its determination must be very rigorous and cautious. In the absence of clear legal provisions or a clear expression of intent by the parties, the principle of relativity of contract should be respected, and the scope of application of joint and several liability should not be expanded arbitrarily in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties.

In conclusion, Jin Century Company requests that the court of second instance find the facts correctly, apply the law properly, and vacate item (4) of the first-instance judgment in accordance with law, thereby reversing the judgment that Jin Century Company bears any liability for payment of project funds.

Jin Century Company, in its response to Bohai Company's appeal, argued: Bohai Company's request that Jin Century Company bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group's repayment of project arrears has no factual or legal basis. There is no expression of intent to form a partnership between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group or Baoyu Company, no partnership agreement was signed, and the relationship does not constitute a partnership-type joint operation. Furthermore, even if it did constitute a partnership-type joint operation, joint and several liability would arise only if the law so provides or the parties so agree.
