This case does not meet those conditions, and Jin Century Company should not bear joint and several liability. Bohai Company's request on appeal to increase the payment of interest and to have Jin Century Company bear the litigation costs has no factual or legal basis. The claim for loss due to work stoppage is not supported by evidence, the claim for a prize for provincial quality project has no factual basis or legal basis, and the parties have no right to appeal the amount of litigation costs. Therefore, all of the above requests are unfounded and should be dismissed.

Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company did not submit a written reply.

Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company agreed with the requests and grounds of Bohai Company's appeal and argued that Jin Century Company should bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group's repayment of project arrears to Bohai Company.

The facts found by this Court in the second instance are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: The construction contracts and supplementary agreements signed by Baoyu Group, Baoyu Company, and Bohai Company are valid. The disputed construction project completed the statutory procedures for project commencement, obtained the "Construction Project Construction Permit," and met the statutory conditions for commencement. The construction unit, Bohai Company, is a professional construction enterprise with a Grade A qualification and possesses the statutory qualifications corresponding to the project. At the time of signing, the parties' expressions of intent were genuine, and the contents did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, it should be determined that the construction contracts and supplementary agreements signed by Baoyu Group, Baoyu Company, and Bohai Company are valid. With respect to issues such as breach of contract and claims, the first-instance judgment has already made determinations, and the rights holders have not appealed these issues. Therefore, the amounts of breach of contract and claims are not within the scope of this Court's review in the second instance.

From the perspective of the evolution of the contracting party: The original Baoyu Company, which was the contracting party under the construction contracts, changed its name to Baoyu Group. Subsequently, Baoyu Group applied to the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce to re-establish Baoyu Company using the original Baoyu Company's qualification certificate. In its application report, Baoyu Group committed to the government authorities: "If any debt issues arise, because the former real estate development company had increased its registered capital to RMB 120 million before changing to Baoyu Group, any debts from this period may be borne by Baoyu Group. Debts from other periods shall still be borne by Baoyu Real Estate. The re-registered Baoyu Real Estate has a registered capital of RMB 15 million, and we guarantee that no harm will be caused to others' interests in matters involving debts." Because the newly established Baoyu Company uses the qualification certificate of the original Baoyu Company, and the two Baoyu Companies have identical names, from an external appearance perspective, it is difficult for the counterparty to the contract to distinguish between the old and new Baoyu Companies. Therefore, in this case, it should be determined that Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company, established jointly with its subordinate units, are the joint contracting parties under the construction contracts. The first-instance judgment correctly made this determination, and this Court affirms it.

In accordance with Article 151 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and in light of the appeal requests of Bohai Company and Jin Century Company, two issues in dispute are identified in this case: (1) whether Jin Century Company should bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of project arrears to Bohai Company; and (2) whether interest should be awarded on the losses due to work stoppage and the prize for quality project. This Court makes the following determinations on the two issues in dispute:

(1) Jin Century Company should not bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of construction arrears to the constructor Bohai Company.

First, Jin Century Company is not jointly and severally liable for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's discharge of the construction arrears to Bohai Company. To begin with, the legal relationship at issue in this case is a construction contract dispute, not a cooperative development real estate contract dispute. The parties to the construction contract in this case are Baoyu Group, Baoyu Company, and Bohai Company, with Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company as the contract-issuing party and Bohai Company as the contractor. The construction contract is binding only on the parties to the contract, i.e., Baoyu Group, Baoyu Company, and Bohai Company, and has no legal effect on persons who are not parties to the contract. The cooperative development relationship between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group does not make Jin Century Company a party to the construction contract, and Jin Century Company should not bear contractual obligations under the construction contract. Second, creditor's rights are relative rights, and relativity is the foundation of creditor's rights. Obligations are legal relationships between specific parties. Both the creditor and the debtor are specific. The creditor can only demand performance from the specific debtor, and the debtor is only obligated to render performance to the specific creditor. Even if a third party's actions prevent the realization of the creditor's right, the creditor cannot, by the force of the creditor's right, demand removal of the obstruction from the third party. Creditor's rights are, by nature, rights in personam. Third, Article 84, paragraph 1, of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Obligations arise either from the provisions of a contract or from the provisions of law. Rights and obligations arise between specific persons." Paragraph 2 provides: "The creditor has the right to demand that the debtor perform his obligations as specified by the contract or as provided by law." The term "specific" means that only the parties to the contract are bound by the content of the contractual rights and obligations. The basis for a creditor's demand that a debtor perform its obligations is either the contract or the law. In this case, Bohai Company argues that Jin Century Company should bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of project arrears. Because there is no "specific" obligation relationship between the parties, and there is no legal basis to pierce the relative effect of the contract, Bohai Company's request on appeal that Jin Century Company bear joint and several liability for the repayment is without legal basis.

Second, there is no fact that Jin Century Company replaced the contract-issuing party under the construction contract or became a joint contract-issuing party with Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company by assuming the performance of the obligation. The first-instance judgment found that acts of Jin Century Company that constituted actual participation in the performance of the construction contract included: the joint construction agreement provided that Baoyu Group and Jin Century Company would jointly select the construction team; and when the constructor requested payment from the construction party, Jin Century Company signed and sealed the "Payment Request Report." This Court holds that the provision in the cooperative development contract regarding joint approval of the construction team and the subsequent expression of intent to recognize the construction contract have no relevance to the purpose of proving that "Jin Century Company actually participated in the performance of the construction contract." Jin Century Company's review of the constructor's "Payment Request Report" was an act to ensure that construction funds were used exclusively for the project, which is an act of performing the cooperative development contract. It cannot, therefore, be deemed that Jin Century Company participated in the performance of the construction contract.

Third, Bohai Company's claim that Jin Century Company should bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of project arrears lacks legal basis. Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over State-owned Land Use Rights Contracts provides: "The term 'cooperative development real estate contract' as used in this Interpretation refers to an agreement whereby the parties agree on the cooperative development of real estate by way of jointly contributing the right to use state-owned land, funds, and other inputs, jointly sharing profits, and jointly bearing risks." The parties to a cooperative development contract each assume their respective rights and obligations as agreed in the contract. "Jointly contributing, jointly sharing profits, and jointly bearing risks" refers to the internal relationship among the cooperative parties, not the external relationship. Article 52 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "If an enterprise or an institution enters into a joint operation with another enterprise or institution and the operation fails to meet the conditions for legal person status, each party to the joint operation shall assume civil liability in proportion to its respective contribution to capital or according to the agreement, with its own property owned or managed. If joint and several liability is to be borne, it shall be borne in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement of the parties." Article 53 provides: "If an enterprise or an institution enters into a joint operation with another enterprise or institution and the parties operate independently according to the agreement, their respective rights and obligations shall be stipulated in the agreement, and each party shall assume civil liability separately." With reference to the above two provisions, the parties in this case did not establish a project company for cooperative development of real estate or form any other organization that does not meet the conditions for legal person status. This should be considered "independent operation," and each party should independently assume civil liability according to the agreement. Furthermore, even if the cooperative development contract between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company falls within the scope of Article 52 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the parties to the joint operation should still bear joint and several liability only in accordance with legal provisions or the agreement. The cooperative development contract between Jin Century Company and Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company is neither an individual partnership nor a partnership enterprise. The provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law or the Partnership Enterprise Law concerning the assumption of joint and several liability by individual partners or general partners should not apply.

The first-instance judgment held that: Because the joint construction benefits had not yet been divided, and the disputed construction project was under Jin Century Company's name, Jin Century Company enjoyed the rights to the work already performed by Bohai Company and obtained benefits from that contract, and therefore should bear joint and several liability. It should be observed that although Jin Century Company received part of the buildings of the disputed construction project as a benefit, this was the reward it obtained for contributing the right to use land. It was a commercial transaction with consideration, not a benefit received without cause.

In conclusion, this Court holds that the part of the first-instance judgment ordering Jin Century Company to bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of a portion of the project arrears to the constructor Bohai Company should be vacated. Bohai Company's request on appeal that Jin Century Company should bear joint and several liability for all project arrears lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. Jin Century Company's request on appeal that it should not bear joint and several liability for Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company's repayment of project arrears to the constructor Bohai Company is established, and this Court supports it.

(2) Bohai Company's request for additional interest on the losses due to work stoppage and the prize for quality project should be supported.

Supreme People's Court, Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Contracts for Construction Project Construction, Article 17 provides: where the parties have agreed on the standard for calculating interest on overdue project payments, such agreement shall govern; in the absence of agreement, interest shall be calculated at the loan interest rate of the same type and for the same period published by the People's Bank of China. Article 18 provides: interest shall be calculated from the date when the project payment becomes due. Pursuant to this provision, the contract-giving party shall pay interest on overdue project payments at the statutory benchmark interest rate. By reference to Article 5 of the Measures for the Administration of Pricing of Construction Project Contracting and Subcontracting of the Ministry of Construction: the bidding base price and bid quotation (project payment) consist of cost (direct costs, indirect costs), profit, and taxes. Direct costs are determined by the consumption of labor, materials, and machinery and their corresponding prices. Indirect costs, profit, and taxes are calculated separately in accordance with relevant regulations. Supreme People's Court, Reply on the Priority of Compensation for Construction Project Payments, Article 3 provides: the construction project payment includes the remuneration of staff, material costs, and other actual expenses that the contractor shall pay for the construction project, but does not include losses caused to the contractor by the contract-giving party's breach of contract. According to the above provisions, the loss due to work stoppage falls under "losses caused by the contract-giving party's breach of contract", and the quality project bonus does not fall within the scope of project payment, so interest should not be calculated under the judicial interpretation in principle. However, in the Agreement signed by both the contract-giving and contract-taking parties on December 1, 2002, it was expressly stipulated that the contract-giving party would compensate the contractor for the loss due to work stoppage caused by its insufficient funds, in the amount of 5.5 million yuan. This amount was the result of several reductions by the contractor on the basis of the claim amount stipulated in the contract. Moreover, the contract also provided that "any loss caused by a further work stoppage due to Baoyu Company's failure to pay compensation on time shall be fully borne by Baoyu Company." Baoyu Company has not paid the loss due to work stoppage as stipulated in the contract, and has also defaulted on a huge amount of project payment, clearly demonstrating its subjective fault of malicious breach of contract. In this case, the judgment only ordering the contract-giving party to pay the principal of the loss due to work stoppage is inconsistent with the contract's provision that the contract-giving party shall compensate for the expanded part of the loss, and it is difficult to make up for the huge economic losses caused to the contractor by the contract-giving party's malicious breach of contract. Accordingly, interest on the loss due to work stoppage paid by the contract-giving party to the contractor shall accrue from the time of project settlement.

On May 18, 2005, Bohai Company and Baoyu Company signed the Bohai Construction Project New Century Home Project Audit Form, and the two parties had no dispute over the project cost of the main structure parts of Buildings 2# and 4#. Pursuant to relevant government documents and contract stipulations, Bohai Company should receive the quality project bonus. To balance the interests of both the contract-giving and contract-taking parties, interest should also accrue from the time of project settlement.

Item (3) of the Civil Judgment No. 3, First Instance (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]) of the Liaoning High People's Court was erroneously expressed, and has been corrected by that court's Civil Ruling No. 3 (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]). This Court recognizes such correction.

Accordingly, Bohai Company's appeal claim that Baoyu Group and Baoyu Company should pay interest on the loss due to work stoppage and the quality project bonus is well-founded, and this Court supports it.

In summary, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 5 of the Civil Judgment No. 3, First Instance (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]) of the Liaoning High People's Court.

2. Amend Item 2 of the Civil Judgment No. 3, First Instance (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]) of the Liaoning High People's Court to: Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, pay to Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company the loss due to work stoppage of 5.5 million yuan, with interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the same type and for the same period published by the People's Bank of China, accruing from May 18, 2005 until the date of full payment.

3. Amend Item 3 of the Civil Judgment No. 3, First Instance (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]) of the Liaoning High People's Court to: Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, pay to Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company the quality project bonus of 799,393.58 yuan, with interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the same type and for the same period published by the People's Bank of China, accruing from May 18, 2005 until the date of full payment.

4. Set aside Item 4 of the Civil Judgment No. 3, First Instance (Liao Min Yi Chu Zi [2006]) of the Liaoning High People's Court.

The burden of the first instance case acceptance fee shall be executed according to the first instance judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee of 192,333 yuan shall be borne by Dalian Bohai Construction Engineering General Company in the amount of 96,166.50 yuan, and jointly by Dalian Baoyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Dalian Baoyu Group Co., Ltd. in the amount of 96,166.50 yuan.

This judgment is final.
